_doc: Heat sources for the heat check (modules/heat.py). Each source kind lists the manifest roles it covers and the temperature a touching printed part can be exposed to (C), every value with its source or marked 'assumption'. `by_part` moves one named part to another kind or to null (not a source). screen: contact_mm = a printed surface point this close to the source surface is 'in contact' (tessellation and sample spacing read up to ~0.3 mm); near_mm = 'within a few mm'; search_mm = largest distance the check measures (farther reads as none). The check measures; it does not decide. temperature_C is the worst case the surface can reach, so a margin is material limit minus it. The hip yaw / roll servo cases carry role purchased_servo_case_family_reference and are servo cases too.

servo_case.temperature_source: Feetech STS3215 datasheet: torque off above 70 C INTERNAL temperature (docs/research/design-checks.md S8). Taken as the case surface worst case: assumption, the case is cooler than the winding, so this over-states the surface

battery_cell.temperature_source: Molicel INR-21700-P50B continuous limit 60 C as set in the old torso thermal_evaluate.py P50B_SPEC.continuous_limit_C (cell can wall at the limit: worst case)

power_board.temperature_source: assumption: hottest part of a loaded buck / precharge board; no measurement or simulation exists (old thermal_evaluate.py models 1.8-11.5 W of board heat in air, not a surface temperature)

compute_board.temperature_source: assumption: SoC heat spreader / board surface of the ROCK 4D compute board under sustained load with its fan; no measurement exists here
